title: The Purpose Of Time-Out
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that knowing how to execute time-out isn't enough — teachers also need to understand its underlying purpose to enforce it with confidence and conviction. He lays out nine purposes in sequence: protecting the right to learn, revoking class membership, sending a message with minimal words, holding students accountable, replacing the need to lecture or berate, allowing time for reflection (recommending at least 15 minutes), allowing for remorse to develop within a trusting relationship, accepting responsibility by requesting to leave, and ultimately changing behavior. He explains that teachers unclear on the 'why' behind time-out are more likely to give in, look the other way, or appear wishy-washy, inviting students to test boundaries. Understanding purpose, he concludes, transforms time-out from a hollow formality into a genuinely behavior-altering experience.
points: Teachers who don't understand the underlying purpose of time-out are more likely to give in, look away, or appear wishy-washy.
Time-out's purposes include protecting the right to learn, revoking class membership, and holding students accountable without personal confrontation.
Time-out should last at least 15 minutes to allow genuine reflection before a student rejoins the class.
Time-out works best within a positive relationship, since real remorse depends on students trusting and admiring their teacher.
A student calling the teacher over to politely request leaving time-out represents accepting responsibility for the misbehavior.
quotes: So many teachers who struggle with classroom management lack an understanding of purpose. In other words, they don’t fully understand the why of what they do.
The most immediate purpose of time-out is to separate the offending student from the rest of the class in order to protect their right to learn.
Time-out is a clear message, best learned by the students themselves, that anyone who interferes with learning is not welcome.
This is one reason why time-out should be at least 15 minutes before allowing the student to rejoin the class.
When you have a positive relationship with your students, when they trust you, admire you, and enjoy being in your class, then they’ll feel remorseful about misbehaving.
Time-out then becomes for your students not just a brief, mindless respite. But a behavior altering experience.
